lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, a normal resting ECG, a normal thallium scan and median test results), the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about {{C07.risk.from|pct}}.

The model adds up two parts: a set of inputs that each add their own amount, and an ST-depression pathway that combines ST depression on exercise with the thallium scan, the resting ECG, resting blood pressure and age.

sentences.text: These add up independently, and more vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raise the predicted risk steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, from about {{C25.risk.from|pct}} at {{C25.statement.change.from}} to about {{C25.risk.to|pct}} at {{C25.statement.change.to}}, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher.

A flat ST segment at peak exercise (rather than an upsloping one) raises it to about {{C26.risk.to|pct}}, and higher serum cholesterol and higher resting blood pressure both raise it steadily: from about {{C27.risk.from|pct}} at {{C27.statement.change.from}} to about {{C27.risk.to|pct}} at {{C27.statement.change.to}}, and from about {{C28.risk.from|pct}} at {{C28.statement.change.from}} to about {{C28.risk.to|pct}} at {{C28.statement.change.to}}.

Being a woman, or having typical angina or non-anginal chest pain rather than no chest pain, lowers it: for an otherwise typical patient, to about {{C31.risk.to|pct}}, {{C29.risk.to|pct}} and {{C32.risk.to|pct}}.

Smaller effects: chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about {{C34.risk.to|pct}}, while a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily (from about {{C35.risk.from|pct}} at {{C35.statement.change.from}} to about {{C35.risk.to|pct}} at {{C35.statement.change.to}}) and {{C36.groups[1].label|text}} lowers it to about {{C36.risk.to|pct}}; resting blood pressure, chest pain type, the thallium result, the resting ECG and age also act through the pathway below.

This part combines ST depression on exercise with the thallium scan, the resting ECG, resting blood pressure and age, and it acts on {{C56.statement.n_active|d}} of {{C56.statement.n|d}} training patients.

Higher ST depression raises the predicted risk slowly at first, then faster, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect: for a typical patient, going from {{C61.statement.change.from}} to {{C61.statement.change.to}} moves it from about {{C61.statement.stronger_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C61.statement.stronger_group.risk_to|pct}} with a reversible defect, and from about {{C61.statement.weaker_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C61.statement.weaker_group.risk_to|pct}} with any other thallium result (for most patients, but for some patients with a normal resting ECG, {{C61.shape.exceptions[0].n_alt|d}} of the {{C61.shape.exceptions[0].n_group|d}} sampled, it rises steadily).

ST depression also raises it more with a normal resting ECG, slowly at first, then faster: from about {{C62.statement.stronger_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C62.statement.stronger_group.risk_to|pct}} over the same range, against about {{C62.statement.weaker_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C62.statement.weaker_group.risk_to|pct}} with any other resting ECG (for most patients, but for some patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan, {{C62.shape.exceptions[0].n_alt|d}} of the {{C62.shape.exceptions[0].n_group|d}} sampled, it rises steadily).

Through this part, ST depression adds to the risk once it rises above about {{C64.statement.threshold}}, and for {{C64.statement.support_check.exceptions|d}} of the {{C64.statement.support_check.n|d}} training patients it already acts below that.

ann_37.text: This part combines two smaller parts, the ST-depression score and the fixed-defect relay, with resting blood pressure, chest pain type, the thallium result and age, and not by simple adding.
It acts on {{C56.statement.n_active|d}} of {{C56.statement.n|d}} training patients, and {{C56.statement.outcome_in_group.positives|d}} of them had heart disease.
For a typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about {{C56.risk.from|pct}} without it and about {{C56.risk.to|pct}} with it.

ann_38.proposed: The model adds two parts: a set of inputs that each add their own amount, led by the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy (for a typical patient, from about {{C01.risk.from|pct}} at {{C01.statement.change.from}} to about {{C01.risk.to|pct}} at {{C01.statement.change.to}}), and a pathway through which higher ST depression on exercise raises the risk slowly at first, then faster.

ann_36.proposed: Each input adds its own amount to the score: more vessels, a flat ST segment, higher cholesterol and higher resting blood pressure raise the predicted risk, and being a woman or having chest pain symptoms lowers it (for an otherwise typical patient, to about {{C31.risk.to|pct}} for a woman and about {{C29.risk.to|pct}} with typical angina).

ann_37.proposed: This pathway raises the predicted risk with ST depression on exercise, slowly at first, then faster, and more with a reversible defect on the thallium scan (from about {{C51.statement.stronger_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C51.statement.stronger_group.risk_to|pct}}, against about {{C51.statement.weaker_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C51.statement.weaker_group.risk_to|pct}}); higher resting blood pressure makes the rise a little smaller, not a large discount.

ann_34.proposed: This part adds risk for ST depression on exercise once it passes about {{C64.statement.threshold}} ({{C64.statement.support_check.exceptions|d}} of {{C64.statement.support_check.n|d}} patients already move below that), rising slowly at first, then faster, and it counts more with a reversible defect on the thallium scan and with a normal resting ECG.

ann_35.proposed: This part passes on whether the thallium scan shows a fixed defect and barely changes the predictions (the largest change in any patient's predicted risk is {{C68.statement.max_change_in_risk|pct}}).
